candidates.title: Cape Breton storm yet another one for the history books
candidates.description: CBC Meteorologist Ryan Snoddon takes a closer look at how much rain fell this past weekend, as well as how it aligned with what the models were predicting.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: It's back to school season. Here's why there's a push to get rid of cars at dropoff and pickup
candidates.description: As the school year starts, the non-profit environmental association Green Communities Canada is continuing its efforts to implement pilot projects clearing regular student dropoff zones of cars.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Belugas transferred from Niagara Falls are under round-the-clock monitoring after deaths: Chicago aquarium
candidates.description: A Chicago aquarium says several of the belugas that were transferred to its site from Ontario's Marineland have health issues.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Quebec overhauled its bottle deposit-refund system. Is it working?
candidates.description: Since the rollout of its first phase in 2023, Consignaction’s bottle deposit-refund system has received mixed reviews from users. Here’s a breakdown of what’s working and what needs improvement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'It's incredible,' Winnipeg man says after car blows over onto someone else's lawn in storm
candidates.description: A Winnipeg man says the damage left by Sunday night's thunderstorm was "overwhelming" after his vehicle rolled into the front yard of a nearby home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Dutch elm disease ravaged Canadian cities. Can we help trees protect themselves?
candidates.description: Scientists in the state of Vermont have spent the summer spreading Dutch elm disease to thousands of trees. It's an experiment to see if a new generation of elms might have resistance to a plague that has been decimating elm populations in the U.S. and Canada for decades.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stephen Fuhr was mocked for opposing the purchase of F-35s. Now he's in charge of Canada's defence procurement
candidates.description: Former RCAF fighter pilot Stephen Fuhr drew mockery from members of the military community after he retired from the Armed Forces in 2009 when he vigorously opposed the purchase of American F-35 aircraft. He's now in charge of Canada's military procurement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why more than 150 years later, Hamilton's Nine Hour Movement still matters
candidates.description: On May 15, 1872, 1,500 workers marched in Hamilton, demanding the workday be reduced to nine hours, a movement that ultimately failed, but paved the way for laws that protect workers today.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Election campaign spotlights Quebec's school system — and whether it's fair to all students
candidates.description: During an education-related announcement on the campaign trail, Coalition Avenir Québec Leader Christine Fréchette said she didn't really believe Quebec's education system was three-tiered. Her comments were made on the heels of a public health report highlighting how the organization of this very system exacerbates health inequalities in young people in Montreal.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Optimism swirls around massive critical metal deposit near Tisdale, Sask., but locals still have questions
candidates.description: Canadian Energy Metals plans to construct a demonstration plant in Tisdale to refine alumina, the critical metal used to create aluminum. The plant could be up and running by 2029 or 2030. The company's CEO says it will eventually look to purchase land in the area for open-pit mining operations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trailblazing Indigenous actor and director Georgina Lightning dead at 63
candidates.description: Indigenous filmmaker and actor Georgina Lightning has died at the age of 63. Her daughter announced the news online late Saturday night, describing the death of her mother as a shocking loss.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'It cannot happen': Why Quebec fans and actors fought to save their own version of The Simpsons
candidates.description: When the beloved Quebec version of the iconic American animated series was cancelled last year, fans rallied to bring it back, not simply because they loved the show, but because they saw Les Simpson as a reflection of what it means to be Québécois.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elbows up or down? Why Alberta is diplomacy-first in the trade war
candidates.description: Nathan Cooper, Alberta’s senior representative to the United States, told CBC’s West of Centre that compared to provinces that have taken a more aggressive approach, Alberta has come out ahead.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sept. 11 was one of many times N.L. residents have opened their homes in a crisis
candidates.description: Newfoundlanders and Labradorians have a long-history of helping those in need, even before the generosity displayed nearly 25 years ago when people opened their homes to stranded airline passengers during 9/11.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 46-year-old Cape Breton woman found dead in flooded area
candidates.description: In a news release issued Sunday, RCMP said the woman's vehicle was parked near her residence in Cleveland, N.S., on the far side of a flooded bridge. First responders carried out a search Saturday and found the body in the area around 2:30 p.m. AT.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'It looked like a puddle': Tow truck driver kept busy by huge N.S. rainfall
candidates.description: Weekends are usually quiet for Tyson McEwan of McEwans Towing, but he has already recovered about 20 vehicles so far this weekend. The Havre Boucher, N.S., business is based in Antigonish County near the Canso Causeway.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Far-right victory in German state expected to send shockwaves throughout the world
candidates.description: Germany’s far-right AfD party won a state election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday. Some experts say the victory sends a message to right-wing populists around the world that the political tides are in their favour.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Investigators to focus on crucial landing moment in Amazon cargo plane crash in Miami
candidates.description: U.S. federal investigators examining why an Amazon cargo jet barrelled off a runway at Miami International Airport and into vehicles, killing at least five people, are likely to focus on a crucial moment in the landing: whether the plane touched down too late to stop safely.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Charles confirms Harry and Meghan to remain non-working royals after their return to U.K.
candidates.description: King Charles authorized a letter to senior British officials on Monday confirming that his youngest son, Prince Harry, and Harry's ‌wife, Meghan, remain non-working royals following their return to the U.K.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli clearance of Gaza rubble could destroy evidence of 'atrocity crimes,' says UN expert
candidates.description: A U.N. expert said on ‌Monday that Israeli clearance of rubble in Gaza could destroy valuable evidence of "atrocity crimes" and prevent the recovery of human remains.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanese town kill 11, state news agency says
candidates.description: Israeli strikes on a southern Lebanese town early on Monday killed at least 11 people including two children and two medics, Lebanon's state news agency said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.K. government slams 'thuggish' anti-migrant protesters, after demonstrators block port
candidates.description: The British government on Monday condemned the "intimidating and thuggish behaviour" of anti-immigrant demonstrators who converged on a port in southern England where migrants were brought ashore after crossing the English Channel.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gloria Steinem on marriage and kids | Throwback
candidates.description: Feminist leader Gloria Steinem died at age 92 on Wednesday. CBC interviewed Steinem several times over the years on a range of topics, including how the women's liberation movement helped her stop feeling guilty about marriage and children.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold talks in Ukraine after meeting with Putin
candidates.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held "encouraging" talks in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push to end more than 4½ years of Russia's full-scale invasion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 5 dead after Amazon cargo plane barrels off Miami runway and smashes into cars: police
candidates.description: An Amazon cargo plane barrelled off a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, killing at least five people as it struck vehicles and burst into flames, authorities said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Far-right AfD wins German state election but falls short of majority
candidates.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged to a resounding victory in a regional election on Sunday but fell a little short of winning a majority in its quest to form the country's first far-right state government since the Second World War.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Reporting on 9/11: The day the world changed
candidates.description: Sept. 11, 2001 started like any other work day in the CBC newsrooms — and then the world changed. Correspondents Adrienne Arsenault, Ioanna Roumeliotis, Paul Hunter and David Common reflect on the chaos and shock of covering 9/11, 25 years later.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman found alive in home destroyed by Nepal flood, days after family began mourning rites
candidates.description: Believing she had perished in Nepal's deadly floods, the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano erupts, cancelling flights at Jakarta airport and others
candidates.description: Anak Krakatau volcano erupted in Indonesia early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic ash drifted across parts of western Indonesia.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran says it will announce new Strait of Hormuz 'exclusion zone'
candidates.description: The new head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council on Sunday said Tehran plans to announce an "exclusion zone" outside the Strait of Hormuz aimed at vessels it believes are attempting to transit the waterway.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The 'shockwaves' of Prince Harry and Meghan's return to the U.K.
candidates.description: Even though there has been much telegraphing of the idea that Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, are not going to be working royals again, their move back to the United Kingdom carries broader implications for both the institution of the monarchy and other members of the Royal Family.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill 4 in southern Lebanon
candidates.description: Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon on Sunday, the Lebanese Health Ministry said, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within areas occupied by its troops.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Etsy seller's 'bruh' T-shirts were removed over a trademark complaint. He says it's trademark squatting
candidates.description: An Etsy seller says the online retailer removed his listings for T-shirts with the word "bruh" after the person who holds a Canadian trademark for it complained. One legal expert worries that the costly nature of trademark disputes makes it difficult to challenge such cases.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Counter-tariffs won't just affect the cost of goods for Canadians. They'll hit the trailers moving them too
candidates.description: Canadians bracing for billions of dollars in counter-tariffs won't just see prices rise on American items like produce, toilet paper and furniture, but on the very semi-trailers used to haul those goods.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Germany's far-right AfD says 'democracy demands' parties work with them after state election win

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thousands turn out in Serbia for funeral of 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladić

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanese village kill 12

candidates.description: Five people died and five others were injured as the Amazon plane overshot the runway after landing at Miami International Airport.

candidates.title: Nepal observes national day of mourning for victims of flash flood disaster

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: China to pump $54bn into state banks and insurers to boost economy
candidates.description: It comes as Beijing is aiming to reshape its economy in the face of a number of challenges.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rescuers dig through debris as seven dead in building collapse in Delhi
candidates.description: It's not clear how many people were inside the building - or if there are still people under the debris.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How significant are AfD's historic gains for Germany and the rest of Europe?

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: India's high-stakes exam system faces a crisis of trust

candidates.title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

candidates.title: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting
candidates.description: One week after the deadly floods, very little is known about China's dead or missing. China's control over media and digital censorship is in stark contrast to open reporting in Nepal.

candidates.description: Germany's populist, far-right Alternative for Germany party has declared victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt after more than doubling its share of the vote in the first of several regional elections this fall.

candidates.title: Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after Moscow Putin meeting
candidates.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held meetings in Kyiv with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy on Sunday, a day after lengthy conversations with Russian President Putin in Moscow.

candidates.title: Trump issues new executive orders on beef sales to pacify American cattle ranchers
candidates.description: President Trump's latest executive orders allows ranchers to sell meat directly to consumers. Ranchers have been upset over Trump's plan to boost beef imports in a bid to lower prices.

candidates.title: Former State Department energy envoy on how the war in Iran is impacting gas prices
candidates.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to former State Department energy envoy David Goldwyn about how the war in Iran continues to affect gas and diesel prices.

candidates.title: The copper peptide trend has gone from creams to injections — ahead of the science
candidates.description: The peptide is supposed to deliver flawless and firm skin, promote wound healing and other anti-aging effects. So what's the evidence behind GHK-Cu?

candidates.title: Pig kidneys keep patients alive long enough to get human kidneys for the first time
candidates.description: For the first time, genetically modified pig kidneys keep two kidney failure patients alive long enough to get human kidneys.

candidates.title: Whatever happened to kindness? Spoiler alert: Our readers prove it's alive and well
